claims.text: Increasing oxygen availability during post-deposition annealing promotes formation of a continuous, load-bearing oxide layer on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The annealing-induced oxide layer acts as a protective barrier that reduces wear rate during 600–800 °C sliding.
The annealing-induced oxide layer limits microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
Processing the FeNiCrCoCu coating under low-oxygen conditions produces a largely metallic, minimally oxidized microstructure.
The controlled intervention is oxygen-rich post-deposition annealing relative to inert or low-oxygen annealing.
The proposed operating regime is sliding at 600–800 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure.
The structural mediator is a continuous, adherent oxide layer containing mixed Mn-, Cr-, and Fe-based spinel or corundum phases.
Enhanced oxygen during annealing facilitates formation of the protective oxide film.
The oxide film bears sliding load.
The oxide film acts as a lubricating tribolayer.
The oxide film suppresses adhesive and abrasive wear mechanisms.
Oxygen-rich annealed coatings will have a lower wear rate than the inert- or low-oxygen-annealed baseline.
Oxygen-rich annealed coatings will have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline.
Oxygen-rich annealed coatings will show less localized plastic deformation, delamination, and debris accumulation than the baseline.
Inert or low-oxygen annealing produces a thinner or patchier oxide than oxygen-rich annealing.
The thinner or patchier baseline oxide causes higher wear and more severe microscopic deformation.
Tribo-oxidation is a dominant wear process for this coating during sliding at 600–800 °C.
The proposed benefit may fail if the oxide cracks or becomes overly brittle under sustained load.
Changes in load or sliding speed may activate different wear mechanisms and invalidate the prediction.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in wear, friction, and microscopic deformation, or observation of degraded performance, is proposed to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The nominal coating contains Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu but no Mn, while the proposed oxide mediator prominently includes Mn-based oxides; no Mn source, contamination route, or substrate contribution is specified.
